Subject: Velora preflight: throughput validation, SLO fit, and fleet schematic

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. To make the Dedicated sizing proposal concrete, we need a short preflight so our capacity team can validate tokens/sec expectations against SLOs. Can you please share the following as a quick attachment (CSV or spreadsheet):

- Typical request size distribution (median, 75p, 95p token counts)
- Percent of requests that use long-context (>= 4k tokens) vs short-context (< 2k)
- Expected peak TPS (requests/sec) and sustained TPS for first 90 days
- Any real example prompts or anonymized payloads that show typical system prompts + user content

If you prefer, Ops can drop the CSV to the Drive link Jonas shared on the call. Our immediate objective: produce a conservative tokens/sec model, map it to p95 latency SLO (1500ms target), and show 1.5x headroom fleet sizing + fallback plan (quantized variants / burst pool).

I'll loop in Ben and Jonas for the sizing sketch. If you want us to run a sample inference trace against a representative payload, we can do that within 48 hours once we have the CSV.

Best,
Kimberly
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks — attached is the CSV with token distributions and a small sample of anonymized prompts. Key notes:
- Median tokens: 420, 75p: 1,100, 95p: 3,700
- ~18% of requests hit long-context (>4k) during batch jobs (nightly enrichment), but the day-to-day product traffic is ~6% long-context
- Expected peak requests/sec for Q1 pilot: 65 rps (API-level), sustained 28 rps
- Typical request includes a system prompt (~120 tokens) + user content (variable)

We also included an ops comment about quiet hours (UTC 02:00–06:00) where heavy batch runs happen — those can be scheduled to dedicated background workers, but they will temporarily increase long-context load.

Files attached: velora_token_profile.csv; sample_prompts.json

—Asha
Product Lead, Velora AI

Subject: Fwd: Velora token profile — quick sizing ask

Ben/Jonas — forwarding Velora's token profile. High-level ask: can you draft a short throughput-to-GPU sketch (p95 latency at 1500ms target) that covers:

1) Production baseline (28 rps sustained; median/95p token split)
2) Peak consumer traffic (65 rps spike) with 6% long-context mix
3) Nightly enrichment window (adds up to 18% long-context for 4 hours) — propose separate burst pool or scheduling mitigation
4) Sizing with 1.5x headroom and fallback options (quantized model version and burst-prewarmed pool)

Priyom — can you include a note about KV cache warmup + cold-start penalty assumptions we should bake into the p95 math?

We need this back to Asha by EOD so they can share with their infrastructure team. Minimal slide or a one-page note is fine.

Thanks — Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha@velora.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 15:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Velora token profile — quick sizing ask

Kimberly / team —

I ran a rapid sketch against our internal perf matrix (Llama-3-style baseline):

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model runtime: 1.9 ms/token (short context paths) on A100-80GB equiv after kernel optimizations
- Long-context penalty: 3.2 ms/token for >4k context due to KV cache spill and attention kernel change
- Average tokens per request: median 420, 75p 1,100, 95p 3,700 (from CSV)
- Concurrency goal: keep p95 latency <= 1500 ms
- Warm caches for 70% of requests after steady-state; cold-start penalty ~250 ms per request when new instance spins up

Sizing outputs (rounded):
- Baseline sustained (28 rps): token/sec ~ (28 * median 420) = 11,760 tps. With 70% cache warm, effective token cost ~= 0.9x runtime — call it 1.7 ms/token avg. Needed CPU/GPU concurrency: ~20 active streams per GPU => about 3 GPUs (A100-equivalent) to keep p95 under 1.5s with 1.5x headroom -> recommend 5 GPUs reserved (dedicated slab)
- Peak spike (65 rps): token/sec spike = 65 * 420 = 27,300 tps (if mix stays median-heavy); with 6% long context and 95p tail events, we'd see p95 stress. For spike protection: keep a 2-GPU warm burst pool (quantized vram-optimized model) + autoscale to up to 8 GPUs transiently. That yields ~1.6–1.8x buffer to absorb brief peaks.
- Nightly enrichment (4h window raising long-context to 18%): schedule enrichment onto separate reserved worker pool (2 GPUs) so it doesn't displace latency-critical traffic; if co-located, add 3 GPUs to main slab for the window.

Attachments: sizing_notes_bencraft.md (brief table + math).

I'll tidy this into one slide. Jonas — can you validate network I/O assumptions for peak (we may need sharding tweaks)?

—Ben

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@velora.ai>, Daniel Simmons <daniel.simmons@velora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Velora preflight: throughput validation, SLO fit, and fleet schematic

Asha / Daniel —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and sample data. Attached is a short one-pager and the conservative sizing sketch Ben produced. TL;DR recommendations:

- Reserve a Dedicated slab of 5 A100-equivalent GPUs for Q1 pilot (covers sustained 28 rps with 1.5x headroom).
- Maintain a 2-GPU warm burst pool with quantized variants for brief spikes up to 65 rps; allow autoscale to 8 GPUs transiently for unusually large tail events.
- Nightly enrichment: run on separate 2-GPU worker pool or schedule into quiet-hours with strict routing to avoid impacting p95.
- KV cache assumptions: Priyom notes a 70% warm-hit expectation after 48 hours of steady traffic; cold-starts add ~250 ms — include a prewarm job during deployments.

Next steps: if this aligns, I'll convert the one-pager into a short commitment annex (with the 5-GPU reserved slab and burst pool described) and send a DocuSign link for signatures. Also flagging we will include a fallback policy: auto-route to quantized model with slightly lower throughput quality if p95 > 2s for more than 3 minutes.

Do you want us to run an empirical trace tomorrow using a sanitized prompt set to verify the 1.9 ms/token baseline? We can schedule a 90-minute window and share the latency traces.

Best,
Kimberly
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
